 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondent, on account of death of Shivakumara, who is husband of petitioner No.1 and father of petitioner No.2, in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 01-11-2023 at about 2:45 p.m., the deceased was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-Y-4321, to go to Nelamangala to Solur.

When he reached NH-75,
Nelamangala-Kunigal road, near Solur Cirlce U-Turn, Solur Town, Magadi Taluk,
Ramanagara District and took U-turn to go to Solur, at that time the driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AG-8404 came on Kunigal main road, with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, recklessly, unmindfully,
without following the traffic rules and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased.
Due to the said impact, the deceased sustained injuries to head, abdomen and all over the body and died on the spot.
Earlier to the accident the deceased was working as cook and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
The Kudur Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

He has admitted that, he is the RC owner of car bearing Reg. No.KA- 03-AG-8404 and the said car was insured with respondent No.2 Iffco Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd., vide policy No.MR935641, valid from 24-11-2022 to 23-11-2023, and the said policy was in force at the time of the alleged accident.

5. Whereas, the respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy bearing No.MR935641 in favour of respondent No.1, in respect of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AG-8404 and its validity from 24-11-2022 to 23-11-2023.
It has denied the involvement of the insured vehicle and manner of accident as alleged in the petition.

Further, it has contended that, the deceased was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05- Y-4321, without having knowledge of riding, without wearing helmet and without possessing valid vehicle documents in a rash and negligent manner, with high speed and he suffered self accident.
The insured vehicle was not at all involved in the alleged accident.

Further it is contended that, during the course of proceedings, if it is proved that the insured vehicle was involved and drivers of both vehicles are responsible for the alleged accident,
the liability may kindly be reduced to the extent of the negligence of the deceased.

Further it is contended that, the petitioners be put to strict proof that, the alleged driver of the insured vehicle and deceased had valid and effective driving licence to drive the class of vehicles at the time of the alleged accident and they were not disqualified to drive the said vehicles.

The respondent No.1 has knowingly entrusted the insured vehicle to the driver who had no valid and effective driving licence and thereby he has consciously breached the terms and conditions of the policy and absolved this respondent from indemnifying the liability, if any, under the alleged cause of action.
Further it is contended that, the alleged driver of the insured vehicle is a necessary party to the proceedings and hence, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary and proper party.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

It has contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provisions under Section 134(c)
and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased.

Further it is contended that, the insured vehicle was plying without valid permit and fitness certificate at the time of alleged accident and the insured had consciously breached the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.

Further in its additional written statement, the respondent No.2 has contended that,
the driving licence of the driver of the insured vehicle i.e. respondent No.1 was expired as on the date of alleged accident.

The respondent No.1 knowing that his driver was not possessing valid and effective driving licence, had consciously allowed him to drive his vehicle and thereby committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy and absolved this respondent from indemnifying the liability, if any, under the alleged cause of action.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 10, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No.KA-03-AG-8404 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the deceased from behind, who came from Tattekere village road and joined Nelamangala-Kunigal main road and was proceeding towards Kunigal.
Further it reveals that, due to said impact, the deceased Shivakumara has sustained grievous injuries on his head and succumbed to said injuries on the spot.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet, which is marked as Ex.P.10, has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No.KA-03-AG-8404 and dashing the same to an ongoing motorcycle of the deceased.

13. At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
the involvement of offending car bearing No.KA-03-AG-8404 in the said accident, the issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

But, the respondent No.1 & 2 have denied the above stated facts and circumstances of the accident and specifically denied that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car.

It is contended that, the deceased while riding his motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-Y-4321 from Nelamangala side, abruptly took right turn near Solur, without observing the vehicular movements on the road and dashed his motorcycle against car bearing No.KA-03-AG- 8404, which was coming from Kunigal side.

Further, they have taken specific defence that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the deceased himself and there was no fault on the part of the driver of offending car.

Further, they have contended that, the petitioners in collusion with the jurisdictional police have falsely implicated the car bearing No.KA-03-AG-8404 in the alleged accident, in order to get wrongful gain from the respondents.
But, the respondents have failed to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of R.W.2, who is the authorised person/Legal Executive of respondent No.2 insurance company and the respondent No.1/R.W.3, who himself is the accused/driver-cum owner of offending car at the time of alleged accident, there is absolutely no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondents to establish to show that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the deceased himself and there was no fault on the part of the driver of offending car.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AG- 8404 and dashing the same to an ongoing motorcycle of the deceased.

Though, the learned counsel for respondents No.1 and 2 have cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her Umadevi vs Vedaprakash M C on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34268811/
5 evidence or which establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the deceased or there was any contributory negligence on the part of the deceased in the cause of accident.

14. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar and Ex.P.4 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on 28 feet wide Nelamangala-Kunigal NH-75 road, near Solur Circle, Magadi Taluk,
Ramanagara District, in between the offending car bearing No.KA-03-AG-8404 and the motorcycle bearing No.KA-05-Y-4321 of the deceased, due to dashing of offending car to the motorcycle of the deceased from behind, who came from Tattekere village road and joined Nelamangala-Kunigal main road and was proceeding towards Kunigal.
Further it is pertinent to note that, as per Ex.P.7 Motor Vehicle Accident report, the said accident has not occurred due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the deceased, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondents to disprove the case of the petitioners and even nothing has been elicited in the cross- examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the deceased or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.
15.

Further, the Ex.P.9 Post-mortem report clearly speaks that, the deceased Shivakumara, has died due to neurogenic shock as a result of injury to vital organ the brain sustained in the road traffic accident.

The investigation officer in his Ex.P.10 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that,
the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No.KA-03-AG-8404 and dashing the same against the motorcycle of the deceased and the deceased Shivakumara has died due to grievous injuries sustained to his head in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the respondent No.1, who is driver cum owner of offending car bearing No.KA-03-AG- 8404.

In such circumstances,
there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, with regard to date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending car bearing No.KA- 03-AG-8404 in the said accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the deceased Shivakumara in the said accident and the cause of his death.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof as in a criminal case are not required."

19. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue, for the reasons stated therein, this Court has already held that, the petitioners have successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that,
the accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No.KA-03-AG-8404 and deceased Shivakumara has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident and succumbed to said injuries, while undergoing treatment.
Now the petitioners are required to establish that, they are the legal representatives of the deceased.
In this regard, they have produced their respective Aadhar cards and Aadhar card of deceased Shivakumara and PAN card of petitioners No.1 and 2, which are marked as Ex.P.11 to 15.
The said documents clearly goes to show that, the petitioner No.1 is wife and petitioners No.2 is the daughter of deceased Shivakumara.

On the other hand, the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased Shivakumara is not specifically denied by the respondents and even there is no rebuttal evidence with respect to same placed on record by the respondents.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the above documents produced by the petitioners and hold that, the petitioners are the legal representatives of deceased Shivakumara.

20. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356, has clearly held that, "The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166(1).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependant on the deceased, would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.
This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra) had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.
The latter part relates to the entitlement of compensation by a person who claims for the same.
It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."

According to the ratio laid down in above decision, the legal representatives though not fully dependent on the deceased are entitled to claim compensation under all the heads i.e., under both conventional and non-conventional heads.

In order to determine the compensation, the age,
avocation, income, dependency, future prospects of the deceased and other conventional heads are to be ascertained.
22. The compensation towards loss of dependency:
The petitioner No.1 is wife and petitioner No.2 is the daughter of deceased Shivakumara.
The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly established that, they are legal representatives of the deceased Shivakumara and they were depending on him.
The dependency does not only mean financial dependency.
Even if the dependency is a relevant criterion to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency is the 'ark of the covenant'.
Dependency includes gratuitous service dependency, physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency.

Hence,
this Court is of the opinion that, all the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
In order to calculate the loss of dependency, the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
i) Age and income of the deceased: The petitioners have averred that, the age of deceased as on the date of accident was 64 years.
To substantiate this point, the petitioners have produced the Aadhar card of deceased Shivakumara, which is marked as Ex.P.13, wherein the year of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 1957.
Admittedly, the accident has occurred on 01-11-2023.
Therefore, as on the date of accident the age of the deceased was 66 years.
It is averred in the petition that, as on the date of accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was working as coolie and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, no document has been produced by the petitioners to show that, the deceased was working as coolie and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

In such circumstances,
there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

a) The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the cases of, G. T. Basavaraj V/s Niranjan and another, in MFA No.7781/2016, judgment dated 11-08-2022, Ramanna and another V/s Y. B. Mahesh and another in MFA No.140/2017, judgment dated 16-01-2020 and New India Assurance Co. Ltd., V/s Anusaya and others in MFA No.101195/2014, judgment dated 05-01-2023, has clearly held that,
"when the income of the deceased is not proved, then the notional income as per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is to be adopted as the income of the deceased."
b) Admittedly, the accident has taken place in the year 2023.

ii) Future prospects:
As on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 66 years.

v) Compensation under conventional heads:
In the present case, admittedly the petitioner No.1 is wife and petitioner No.2 is the daughter of deceased Shivakumara.
Hence, the petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for compensation under the head of spousal and parental consortium.

As per the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the compensation under the following conventional heads is awarded:
a) Loss of estate - Rs. 15,000/-

Therefore, the compensation under the above conventional heads is enhanced by 20%, the loss of estate comes to Rs.18,000/-, the loss of spousal and parental consortium comes to Rs.48,000/- each to petitioners No.1 and 2 and funeral expenses comes to Rs.18,000/-.

24. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of offending car bearing No.KA-03-AG-8404.
As per Ex.R.4, the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2, bearing No.MR935641 was valid from 24-11-2022 to 23-11- 2023.
As such, the said policy was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 01-11-2023.

Further,
the evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AG-8404 the said accident has occurred and the deceased Shivakumara has succumbed to grievous injuries sustained in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.

The respondent No.2 being the insurer of said vehicle is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.
25.

But, the respondent No.2 has taken specific defence that, as on the date of accident the respondent No.1/driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AG-8404 was not holding valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle.

As there is breach of fundamental condition of the policy,
the respondent No.2 insurance company is not liable to indemnify the insured/respondent No.1.

In such circumstances, the burden was on the respondent No.1 to establish that, as on the date of accident he was holding valid & effective driving licence to drive the offending car, which he has failed to discharge in the present case.

26. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 vehemently argued that, as per the Ex.P.10 final report/charge-sheet, at the time accident the respondent No.1/driver of offending car bearing Reg.

As rightly argued by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2, as per the Ex.P.10 final report/charge- sheet, at the time accident the respondent No.1/driver of offending car bearing Reg.

11 No.KA-03-AG-8404 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle and hence in addition to the offence punishable under Sec.279 and 304(A) of I.P.C., he has been charge- sheeted for offence punishable U/Sec.181 of Motor Vehicles Act and admittedly the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the respondent No.1, who is the drive cum owner of the offending car.
Further, the respondent No.1 has not produced any document to show that, as on the date of accident he was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the offending car.

Further it is pertinent to note that, the respondent No.1 in his reply to notice issued under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act, which is marked as Ex.P.6, has clearly stated that, he was holding driving licence from 23-06-2003 to 22-06-2023, but as on the date of accident the said licence had expired.
The same is deposed by the respondent No.1/R.W.3 in his evidence also.

Further, the R.W.1 has deposed in his evidence that, the licence holder by name Veda Prakash/respondent No.1 was holding LMV (NT) driving licence, it was valid from 23-06- 2003 to 22-06-2023 and the said licence was renewed on 22- 11-2023.

Further he has deposed that, the same was not renewed in the gap period from 22-06-2023 to 22-11-2023 and the said licence holder has not filed any application to their R.T.O., office to renew his licence in between the period from 22-06-2023 to 22-11-2023.
This clearly goes to show that, as on the date of accident i.e. 01-11-2023, the driver of the offending car was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
But, in terms of proviso to Sec.14 of Motor Vehicles Act, every driving licence, notwithstanding its expiry, continuous to be effective for a period of 30 days from such expiry.

Likewise, Sec.15(1) of Motor Vehicles Act prescribes that, on an application being made, the licensing authority shall renew the driving licence with effect from the date of its expiry, however, if an application is made more than 30 days after date of the expiry, the driving licence shall be renewed with effect from the date of its renewal.

29. In the present case, admittedly the licence held by the petitioner to drive Light Motor Vehicle (NT) was valid for the period from 23-06-2023 to 22-06-2023, the same had expired on 22-06-2023 and it was renewed on 23-11-2023 for further period from 23-11-2023 till 22-11-2033.

Further,
admittedly the said licence was not renewed in between the gap period from 22-06-2023 to 22-11-2023.

As per the proviso to Sec.14 & Sec.15(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, every driving licence,
notwithstanding its expiry, continuous to be effective for a period of 30 days from such expiry and on an application being made, the licensing authority shall renew the driving licence with effect from the date of its expiry, however, if an application is made more than 30 days after date of the expiry, the driving licence shall be renewed with effect from the date of its renewal.
But, in the instant case there is no material placed on record by the respondent No.2 to show that, on what date the respondent No.1 has applied for renewal of his licence.
Whether he has applied within 30 days from the date of expiry or he has applied after expiry of 30 days grace period for renewal.

30. Further, it is pertinent to note that, the R.W.1 has denied the suggestions made in cross-examination that, the respondent No.1 had approached their RTO office for renewal of licence on 22-06-2023 and requested to renew the same, but, on the said date they have refused to receive his application stating that, there is non-availability of smart card to renew the licence and directed him to apply on some other day.

Further he has denied that, the respondent No.1 had approached their office 2 to 3 times with a request to renew his licence and stating the above reason they have postponed to renew his licence and finally it was renewed on 23-11-2023.

Though, the R.W.1 has denied the above suggestions, there is no document produced by him to show that, the respondent Umadevi vs Vedaprakash M C on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34268811/
12 No.1 has applied for renewal of licence after expiry of 30 days grace period.

There is no material placed on record by the respondent No.2 to show that, the date of application on the basis of which the licence of respondent No.1 was renewed for the period from 23-11- 2023 till 22-11-2033, was not within the period of 30 days from the date of expiry or the same has been applied after the date of accident i.e. 01-11-2023.
The date of application on which the respondent No.1 has applied for renewal of his licence does not find place even in Ex.R.2 Extract of Driving Licence.

In such circumstances, it leads this Court to draw adverse inference against the respondent No.2 and hold that, the respondent No.1 has applied for renewal of his licence well within the period of limitation and the same has not been renewed by the concerned R.T.O., in time.

31 . Further, it is pertinent to note that, it is not the case of the respondent No.2 that, the respondent No.1 had never held the driving licence to drive the light motor vehicle or he was not having knowledge to driver the light motor vehicle especially car or he was disqualified from holding or obtaining a driving licence to driver light motor vehicle.

The mere contention of the respondent No.2 is that, the respondent No.1 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the offending car, as on the date of accident, as the driving licence held by him has expired on 22-06- 2023, much prior to the date of accident.

Mere because of expiry of the period of licence and the omission of the driver to get licence renewed within the period of limitation, it cannot be said by any stretch of imagination that, there is breach of condition of the policy, for which the insurance company can be exonerated from the liability to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

Therefore,
in such circumstances and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the opinion that, the liability of the respondent No.2 insurance company to indemnify the insured or to pay compensation to the third party, cannot be absolved under Sec.149(2)(ii)(a) of Motor Vehicles Act.

As such, the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 does not hold good and the ratio laid down in the above cited decisions relied by him in support of his arguments are not applicable to the given facts and circumstances of the accident in question.

On the other hand the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the petitioners and respondent No.1 hold good and the findings given in the above cited decisions relied by the learned counsel for petitioners are aptly applicable to the facts and circumstances of the present case.
Accordingly, it is held that, there is no breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the respondent No.1.
As such, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AG-8404 has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

Therefore, holding that, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.7,72,000/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
32. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.7,72,000/- (Rupees seven lakh seventy two thousand only), with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.

23. Accordingly, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
